fixtures.text: San Francisco's amendments to Chapter 4 of the plumbing code add only Section 405.4 (no toilet-sink combinations where treated alternate water piping is used) and Section 415.2.1 (drink tap stations). Section 422 and Table 422.1 are not amended, so the state's counts and the state pack's worked examples stand. DBI Information Sheet P-04 (2025-07-11) confirms that DBI uses California Plumbing Code Section 422 and Table 422.1, says which projects must calculate the counts, and says DBI works out occupant load from California Building Code Table 1004.5 unless the designer asks to use California Plumbing Code Table 4-1 with an AB-005 request.
fixtures.quote: Chapter 4 PLUMBING FIXTURES AND FIXTURE FITTINGS SECTION 405 - PROHIBITED FIXTURES 405.0 Add the following section: 405.4 Watercloset-Sink Combinations. Watercloset-Sink combinations are not allowed in structures with treated alternate water piping. SECTION 415.0 - DRINKING FOUNTAINS 415.2 Add the following section: 415.2.1 Drink Tap Stations. New construction that provides one or more drinking fountains shall provide a Drink Tap Station per San Francisco Environment Code Section 2304.

other_quotes.quote: The California Plumbing Code Section (CPC) 422.0 is used to determine the minimum number of plumbing fixtures required for each type of building occupancy. ... Architects or engineers may choose to use the occupant load factor from California Building Code Table 1004.5 or CPC Table 4-1 for determining occupant loads for plumbing fixture counts only. ... DBI plan checkers will default to choosing CBC Table 1004.5 in occupant load determinations for calculating plumbing fixtures if this alternate code path is not called out on the plan submittal by the design team and if the AB-005 is not received as part of the plan submittal.

According to CPC Table 422.1, Minimum Plumbing Facilities, plumbing fixture count calculations are required for all new buildings, first time tenant improvements, tenant enlargements, changes in occupancy and additions. Existing plumbing fixture counts are not required to be recalculated when the above scenarios do not apply.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Not redone: the table is the state's, so the state pack's rows (by number of occupants) apply. What differs in San Francisco is how the occupant number is worked out from floor area: DBI defaults to the building code's table, and the plumbing code's table (150 sq ft per person for offices, 30 for restaurants and classrooms, as in the state pack) is used only on request. The building code's floor-area figures were not read, so the page gives no numbers for them. The 50-person single-restroom statement comes from the state plumbing code as read for the California pack.

restrooms_city.rule: San Francisco Ordinance 53-16 (2016) added Police Code Section 3305.3: every single-user toilet facility in a business or place of public accommodation that is open to the public or to employees must be identified as all-gender by a compliant sign and be available to people of any gender identity; multi-user rooms may be all-gender but need not be. The Department of Building Inspection verifies the signs on complaint and during regular interior inspections, and a failure is a Building Code violation. The same ordinance added Administrative Code Section 4.1-3: buildings on land the City owns, or leased to or by the City, need at least one all-gender toilet facility on each floor where toilets are required or provided, in new construction and on floors that are extensively renovated; where such a building has five or more multi-user toilet facilities, at least one is identified as all-gender. This overlaps the state's single-user rule and adds the city enforcement route and the city-building rule.
restrooms_city.quote: SEC. 3305.3. ALL-GENDER TOILET FACILITIES. (a) Requirement. All toilet facilities in any business establishment or place of public accommodation including those in or on City-owned buildings or property, whether existing or proposed, that are (1) single-user toilet facilities and (2) open to the public or to the employees of the establishment or public accommodation shall be identified as all-gender by signage that complies with either Title 24 of the California Code of Regulations or the Federal Americans with Disabilities Act and made available to persons of any gender identity. Multiple-user toilet facilities may be identified as all-gender facilities but are not required to be identified as all-gender. ... SEC. 4.1-3 ... (a) New Construction. At least one all-gender toilet facility shall be provided on each floor in any new building constructed on City-owned land or that is constructed by or for the City where toilet facilities are required or provided. ... (b) Existing Buildings. Unless not allowed by an existing lease, whenever extensive renovations are made on one or more floors in any building on land that the City owns or in a building that is leased to or by the City, at least one all-gender toilet facility shall be provided on each floor where the renovations take place and toilet facilities are required or provided.

other_quotes.quote: When located within any business establishment, place of public accommodation, or state or local government agency, single accommodation restrooms must not be defined as gender specific within San Francisco and the State of California. ... Gender-specific multi-accommodation "women's" and "men's" restrooms are still allowed at both the local and state level.

All single-user restrooms in any business or establishment that are open to the public or employees must comply. Existing single-user restroom facilities are required to replace any gender specific signage indicating that the facility is open to all persons.

restrooms_city.note: The ordinance was read as enacted in 2016. The current codified text of Police Code Section 3305.3 and Administrative Code Section 4.1-3 (code library, blocked) was not read; DBI Information Sheet DA-16 (2025-03-24) and the city's ordinance page show the single-user rule is still applied.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to San Francisco job sites. Price your restroom in five questions and see the California and city rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for San Francisco offices, hotels, restaurants and hospitals, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** San Francisco uses California's rules, which set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** San Francisco's list of work that needs no building permit includes "movable cases, counters and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches (1753 mm) high" and "painting, papering and similar finish work". It doesn't name toilet partitions, so ask the Department of Building Inspection (628-652-3200) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a one-person restroom must be signed as all-gender. San Francisco's own ordinance requires the same of every one-person restroom open to the public or to employees, and the Department of Building Inspection checks the signs during inspections. A shared all-gender room is allowed in place of separate men's and women's rooms if every toilet is in a floor-to-ceiling privacy compartment whose door locks from the inside and shows when it's occupied. Buildings on land the city owns or leases need at least one all-gender restroom on each floor when they are built or extensively renovated.
page.confirm_office: the San Francisco Department of Building Inspection
page.stalls_intro: San Francisco counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and California's rules require urinals in the men's room. Every toilet needs a stall, and urinals need screens between them. The women's room must have at least as many toilets as the men's room has toilets and urinals together.
page.stalls_after: San Francisco applies these minimums to new buildings, first-time tenant build-outs, tenant expansions, changes of use and additions. Other projects don't have to recalculate the number of toilets. An office or shop with 50 people or fewer may have a single one-person restroom. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, San Francisco's plan checkers use the building code's floor-area figures. Your architect can ask to use the plumbing code's figures instead: one person per 150 square feet of office floor, and one per 30 square feet of restaurant dining room or classroom. Your architect or the San Francisco Department of Building Inspection sets the final number.
page.install_rule: To file permits online in San Francisco, a contractor registers with the Department of Building Inspection using a California contractor license, a San Francisco business registration certificate and proof of workers' compensation cover. California requires its contractor license, usually the C-61/D-34 class, for partition installs of $1,000 or more, and at any price when the job needs workers or a permit. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: In San Francisco the contractor needs a California contractor license for jobs of $1,000 or more.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** California requires the state-set wage on public jobs over $1,000, including city and school district work. For a carpenter in San Francisco County that is $74.46 an hour plus $34.95 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.625% in San Francisco: 7.25% statewide, 0.5% for the Bay Area Rapid Transit District, 0.5% for the county transportation authority, 0.25% for the county public finance authority and 0.125% for the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hotels and event venues:** stainless steel or phenolic that stands up to heavy daily use.
